key_insight: A bilevel DLMP-based controller coordinates EV active/reactive charging under uncertainty, using a compact robust reformulation to keep costs low while supporting voltage stability in distribution networks.
engineering_relevance: The framework offers a practical, computation-efficient way to integrate EV fleets and reactive power support into distribution operation without relying on large scenario sets.
method: Upper level: EV aggregator schedules active and reactive charging to minimize charging cost.
Lower level: network-constrained dispatch computes DLMPs while enforcing feeder and voltage limits.
Uses a deterministic robust counterpart for normal-minus-beta net-demand uncertainty, with KKT/Big-M reformulation and exact DLMP preservation.
evidence_signal: Simulations on the IEEE 33-bus distribution system show improved voltage security, uncertainty-aware EV coordination, and much lower computational complexity than stochastic and conventional robust methods.
watch_item: The method depends on accurate uncertainty modeling and on a valid Big-M/KKT reformulation, which can be sensitive to parameter tuning and network-specific assumptions.
paper_title: Scenario-Free Uncertainty-Aware DLMP-Based Bilevel Coordination of EV Charging and Reactive Power Support in Distribution Networks
